# Sirach Chapter 42 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 42 | **Date:** 2026-03-17

---

**42:1** Do not be ashamed of these things, and do not show partiality in a way that leads to sin:

**42:2** of the law of the Most High and his covenant, and of pronouncing judgment that vindicates the ungodly;

**42:3** of settling accounts with a business partner and with traveling companions, and of dividing a property inheritance;

**42:4** of accurate scales and weights, and of acquiring much or little;

**42:5** of profit from dealing with merchants, and of frequent discipline of children, and of flogging a dishonest servant until he bleeds.

**42:6** Where there is a wicked wife, a seal is advisable; and where there are many hands, lock things up.

**42:7** Whatever you entrust to others, let it be counted and weighed; and put everything given and received in writing.

**42:8** Do not be ashamed to instruct the ignorant and the foolish, or the elder who is judged by the young. Then you will truly be educated and approved in the sight of every living person.

**42:9** A daughter is a hidden anxiety to her father, and worry about her robs him of sleep: lest in her youth she wither before her time; when married, lest she be hated;

**42:10** while still a virgin, lest she be defiled and become pregnant in her father's house; while living with a husband, lest she prove unfaithful; or after marriage, lest she be barren.

**42:11** Keep a strict watch over a headstrong daughter, lest she make you the laughingstock of your enemies, a subject of talk in the city and a reproach among the people, and put you to shame in the public assembly.

**42:12** Look upon no man for his good looks, and do not sit in the company of women;

**42:13** for from garments comes the moth, and from a woman comes a woman's wickedness.

**42:14** Better is the wickedness of a man than a woman who does a kindness — and indeed a woman who brings shame and disgrace.

**42:15** Now I will call to mind the works of the Lord, and what I have seen I will recount. By the word of the Lord his works came into being.

**42:16** The shining sun looks down upon everything, and the work of the Lord is full of his glory.

**42:17** Even to his holy ones the Lord has not granted power to recount all his wonders, which the Lord Almighty has established, so that the universe might stand firm in his glory.

**42:18** He searches out the abyss and the human heart; he understands their every cunning design; for the Most High knows all knowledge, and he observes the signs of the age,

**42:19** declaring what has passed and what is to come, and revealing the traces of hidden things.

**42:20** No reflection escapes him, and nothing is hidden from him.

**42:21** He has arranged the magnificent works of his wisdom; he is from everlasting to everlasting. Nothing can be added to him or taken away, and he has no need of any counselor.

**42:22** How beautiful are all his works, worth contemplating even to the smallest spark!

**42:23** All these things endure forever; they are preserved for all eternity; all of them obey him in every need.

**42:24** All things come in pairs, one the counterpart of the other, and he has made nothing incomplete.

**42:25** Each reinforces the goodness of the other, and who could ever have enough of seeing his glory?
